title: Seedlet Atelier Daybook
content:
Quick notes + working experiments for small-shot prompt templates (seedlet concept). Mostly personal scratchpad. Goal: compact templates that generalize across classification, extraction, and short-form generation while being robust to token budget and reranking artifacts.

High-level hypotheses (working):
- Few exemplars that emphasize *contrastive negatives* (one good, one bad) yield more stable outputs than 3 positive-only exemplars for edge-case instructions.
- Short explicit rubric lines ("If output missing -> return "MISSING"") reduce hallucinated fillers in extraction tasks.
- Steering by role-play label ("You are a terse assistant") + temperature 0.2 often beats more complex framing for constrained-format outputs.

Open questions:
- How brittle are single-token sentinel responses across quantized models (4-bit)? (observe difference between 4-bit GPT-like and 8-bit Llama variants)
- Do we need to canonicalize negative examples to avoid accidental pattern-matching?

TODOs:
- [ ] Convert top-3 templates into tests in prompt-benchmarks PR (linked).
- [ ] Add small rubric set for extraction tasks: presence/format/validity.
- [ ] Run 100-shot Monte Carlo with random seed order to check exemplar-order sensitivity.

Template bank (compact forms, experiment codes inline):
1) SEEDLET-CLF-1 (classification, 2-shot contrastive)
Prompt: "You are an assistant that answers in one of [POSITIVE, NEUTRAL, NEGATIVE]. Example 1 (GOOD): Text: "I loved the new feature." -> POSITIVE. Example 2 (BAD): Text: "User said it broke." -> NEGATIVE. Now classify: Text: "{INPUT}" ->"
Notes: try with temperature 0.0 and 0.2, top_p 0.9.

2) SEEDLET-EXT-1 (extraction, sentinel guarded)
Prompt: "Extract the email addresses from the text. If none, respond EXACTLY: MISSING. Output JSON with key "emails" and array value. Example: "Contact: jane@acme.com" -> {"emails": ["jane@acme.com"]}. Now extract: "{INPUT}" ->"
Notes: attention to final token; append explicit "END" sentinel in some runs to avoid trailing commentary.

3) SEEDLET-SUM-TRIM (short summary, 1-shot with rubric)
Prompt: "Summarize the following in at most 25 words. Use neutral tone. If the text is less than 10 words, quote it verbatim. Text: "{INPUT}" ->"
Failure-case observed: model often expands verbatim short texts unless rubric includes length check. Add "If length < 10: QUOTE" guard.

Few-shot set examples (kept low-cost intentionally):
- EX1 (pos/neg contrast): "Loved the onboarding, intuitive and fast. -> POSITIVE"; "Crashes on save, lost work. -> NEGATIVE"
- EX2 (email extraction): "Reach out: support@foo.io and sales@foo.io -> [support@foo.io, sales@foo.io]"
- EX3 (summary): "Launch delayed by two weeks due to infra -> Delayed by two weeks due to infra issues"

Failure modes observed in quick runs (notes):
- Soft-coverage drift: when exemplars include different label wording (Great vs Loved) model maps unevenly; standardize lexicon.
- Hallucinated field values: extraction template occasionally fabricates plausible-looking emails for ambiguous tokens (e.g., "john at example" -> john@example). Add explicit "only exact matches" phrasing.
- Over-literal repetition: when rubric says "quote verbatim", longer models sometimes paraphrase. Try exact-token anchors ("QUOTE_START" / "QUOTE_END").

Quick parameter matrix I ran (small results summary):
- model: redwood-7b-q4 / temp:0.0 / exemplars:2 contrast -> classification accuracy on small dev 0.82.
- model: redwood-7b-q4 / temp:0.2 / sentinels on / extraction exact -> precision 0.96, recall 0.88 (misses obfuscated emails).
- model: guanaco-13b / temp:0.0 / 3-pos exemplars -> classification 0.78, more variance by exemplar order.

Micro-experiments to run (next runs):
- Replace negative exemplar with synthetic adversary (mildly contradictory phrasing) to measure robustness.
- Test explicit "NO_INFER" guard for extraction that forbids inference-based correction.
- Try 0-shot vs 1-shot where the single shot is the negative example (weird but promising in early tests).

Notes-to-self about formatting heuristics:
- Keep single-line exemplar separators (
) instead of paragraphs to reduce model's tendency to create numbered lists.
- Use all-caps sentinel tokens for missing/invalid signals (MISSING, NO_MATCH, QUOTE_START) — empirically easier to parse downstream.
- Avoid mixing JSON-output instruction with conversational framing in same prompt; if must combine, put JSON schema at the very end.

Lightweight evaluation rubric (to add to test harness):
- Presence: Did the response include required fields? (Y/N)
- Format: Valid JSON / CSV / expected token format? (Y/N)
- Fidelity: Do extracted values match gold exactly? (precision score as float)
- Hallucination: False values introduced? (count)
- Verbosity: tokens used (int)

Misc notes and breadcrumbs:
- Slack thread: #prompt-garden March 2026 has convo re: sentinel strategies (link can be pulled).
- Keep versions: seedlet-v1 (current), seedlet-v1b (adds NO_INFER), seedlet-v2 (contrastive triplet variant).

End of day log (2026-03-10): small wins: contrastive 2-shot reduces edge-case flips in classification dev set; reminder to lock exemplar lexicon and add explicit "no guessing" line for extraction.

Rough log of prompts to commit to PR:
- SEEDLET-CLF-1 (as-is)
- SEEDLET-EXT-1 (add NO_INFER variant)
- SEEDLET-SUM-TRIM (add QUOTE anchors)

Random scribbles: "try anchor-first ordering for exemplars -> anchor = negative example at position 1"; "consider tiny preface: "Model: do not invent answers" as a micro guard"

If I step away for a week: push the three templates above into prompt-benchmarks/seedlet folder, add the tiny rubric, then run nightly with 50 random seeds to estimate exemplar-order variance.

-- A.P.
